title: Loop Polarity Tracer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
System Dynamics
Causal Loop Diagram
Polarity Link
Reinforcing Loop
Balancing Loop
description: A vis-network causal loop diagram of two learner loops that share the Mastery variable. Learners trace each loop one link at a time, count its negative links, classify it as reinforcing or balancing, and flip link signs to watch the loop label change.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Classifying feedback loops by counting negative polarity links
learningObjectives: The learner will examine a causal loop diagram, trace its polarity links, and determine whether the loop is reinforcing or balancing.
prerequisites: Feedback loop, polarity link and causal loop diagram (Chapter 8)
Reading arrows in a network diagram

accessibility.notes: All controls are native buttons, a select and a checkbox; the details panel is an aria-live region; polarity is shown by symbol (+ or minus) as well as color and flipped links are dashed

dataFiles: Causal loop JSON (metadata, nodes, edges, loops) embedded at the top of loop-polarity-tracer.js

controls.label: Trace next link
controls.purpose: Highlight the next link around the chosen loop and update the negative-link counter

controls.label: Reinforcing / Balancing
controls.purpose: Classify the loop before its final link is revealed

controls.label: Flip a sign
controls.purpose: Clicking a link reverses its polarity; loop markers update between R and B

controls.label: Restore signs
controls.purpose: Return every link to its original polarity

controls.label: + / - / Fit
controls.purpose: Zoom and re-fit the diagram (mouse-wheel zoom is disabled)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided tracing with a commit-before-reveal classification and a what-if sign flip
keyQuestions: How many negative links does each loop contain?
Why does an odd count of negative links make a balancing loop?
What happens to a loop's type when you flip one link? Two links?
commonMisconceptions: A loop with any negative link is balancing (only an odd count is)
Polarity describes the size of an effect (it describes only its direction)
A reinforcing loop always means growth (it can amplify a decline too)
assessmentOpportunities: Accuracy of the Reinforcing/Balancing choice before the final link
Explanation of the result of a two-link flip
